title: perf(canary): enhanced auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve reliability of automated performance canaries by making the detector more robust to noise and adding rollout guards that prevent automatic promotion of variants when intermittent regressions are detected. This PR implements a multi-signal detector (latency + throughput + p99 jitter) with hysteresis and a configurable suppression window, plus controller-side rollout guards that require sustained improvement before a canary is promoted.

What changed (high level):
- Add multi-signal detection pipeline: latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, and jitter-based anomaly scoring.
- Introduce hysteresis thresholds and suppression windows to avoid flip-flopping on transient spikes.
- Controller changes: require N consecutive successful checks (configurable) and minimum sample size before promotion.
- Add safety policy: emergency fallback route and automatic rollback when sustained regression is detected post-rollout.
- Observability: new metrics (canary_detector_score, canary_suppression_active, canary_promotions_attempted), dashboards, and detailed debug logs.
- Tests: unit + e2e perf-canary integration tests with synthetic workloads.
- Docs: updated runbook and rollout guide.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1258)
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests added and run in perf lab
- [x] Updated monitoring dashboards and alerting rules
- [x] Release notes entry included

Testing and validation:
- Ran the perf-canary in the benchmark lab against 3 workload shapes (chat low-latency, long-seq generation, high-throughput embeddings). The detector correctly suppressed promotion on short 10s spikes while allowing promotion for improvements sustained for >= 3 minutes.
- CI: initial run had a flaky e2e test (timing); fixed by increasing controlled sample window and re-running. Final CI status is green.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to perf-canary namespace for 48 hours, followed by gradual enablement in canary controller for low-traffic routes. We will monitor canary_detector_score, canary_promotions_attempted, and on-call alerts for 72 hours after enablement.

Notes: The new default hysteresis parameters are conservative; teams can tune per-workload via canary config. See configs/docs/perf-canary.md for examples.

release_notes: Improved perf canary detection: multi-signal detection (latency/throughput/jitter), hysteresis and suppression windows to reduce noisy promotions, controller rollout guards requiring sustained success before promotion. Teams can tune parameters per-canary. Refer to docs/perf-canary.md for configuration and rollout guidance.
additional_context: Related to ongoing perf effort (ENG-1258) to reduce false-positive canary promotions and ENG-1302 for rollout safety. This addresses customer incidents where transient infra noise caused premature promotions. No breaking changes to public APIs.
